points.name: Strontia Springs Sentinel Gauge
points.usgs_name: SOUTH PLATTE RIVER ABV STRONTIA SPGS RESERVOIR, CO
points.blurb: The sentinel. The last measurement point before 80% of Denver's water enters Strontia Springs Reservoir. Reads temperature, conductance, dissolved oxygen, pH, and turbidity every 15 minutes. Water passing here takes about four days to reach the plant intake (Denver Water's own figure), mostly resting in the reservoir; that transit time is the warning window a soft sensor tries to use. In the August 2026 storm, evening rain became a 329 FNU spike here by 1:45 AM while the flow gauge upstream barely moved: the sediment washed in from side canyons between the two, the stretch no gauge watches.

points.name: South Platte Gauge near Trumbull
points.usgs_name: SOUTH PLATTE RIVER BLW BRUSH CRK NEAR TRUMBULL, CO
points.blurb: Nearest upstream flow gage to Strontia Springs, below Brush Creek near Trumbull. This is where the August 2026 storm pulse was measured.

points.name: Foothills Treatment Plant
points.blurb: Denver Water's largest treatment plant. Receives Strontia Springs water through Conduit 26, treats it, and sends it to the city.

points.name: Marston Treatment Plant
points.blurb: Treats South Platte water delivered by gravity through Conduit 20, plus Strontia Springs water.

points.name: Northwater Treatment Plant
points.blurb: The new north system plant beside Ralston Reservoir, treating Moffat Tunnel water. Successor to the 1937 Moffat plant.

points.name: Moffat Treatment Plant
points.blurb: The 1937 north system plant in Lakewood, being retired as Northwater takes over its role.

points.name: Strontia Springs Dam
points.blurb: The 243-ft dam in Waterton Canyon that 80% of Denver's water passes through. Diverts to the Foothills and Marston plants. Aurora draws its supply here too.

points.name: Marston Diversion Dam
points.blurb: The second, smaller intake 2.6 miles below Strontia Springs Dam. Feeds Conduit 20, which flows by gravity to Marston Lake.

lines.name: Roberts Tunnel
lines.blurb: 23 miles under the Continental Divide. Carries Dillon Reservoir water east to the North Fork of the South Platte at Grant. Straight line drawn between the verified portals.

lines.name: Moffat Water Tunnel
lines.source: Portals from OpenStreetMap ways 626775058/17053656 (the rail tunnel the water tunnel parallels); west end matches USGS gage 09023562 within 70 m.
lines.blurb: 6.2 miles under the divide at Winter Park, beside the railroad tunnel. Carries Fraser basin water east into South Boulder Creek, bound for Gross Reservoir.

lines.name: Conduit 26
lines.blurb: 3.7 miles of 120-inch pipe from Strontia Springs Dam to the Foothills plant. Capacity 750 million gallons a day. At that full capacity the published diameter and flow work out to about 15 ft/s, so water leaving the dam is only about 20 minutes from the plant. The slow part comes before: from the sentinel gauge, through the reservoir, to the intake takes about four days.

lines.name: Conduit 20
lines.blurb: Gravity conduit from the Marston Diversion Dam in Waterton Canyon to Marston Lake inside Denver.
